articles.content: The starting gun of the Oscar season starts Monday, and by next Sunday, it will have a shape that many of us will be able to see clearly. For months, the Oscar race has run on festival premieres, studio screenings and ever more elaborate predictions, mine included. This week, the people with ballots finally speak. The Gothams, the New York Film Critics Circle, the National Board of Review, the American Film Institute and LAFCA each answer to a different electorate and each has its own complicated history with the Academy. None of them pick the Oscars, but they all shape the conversation that follows. The question isn’t only who wins. It’s who wins where, and what each victory says about the corner of the electorate that handed it out. Monday, Nov. 30: Gotham Awards Tuesday, Dec. 1: New York Film Critics Circle Awards Wednesday, Dec. 2: Film Independent Spirit Awards nominations Wednesday, Dec. 2: National Board of Review Awards Thursday, Dec. 3: AFI Awards honorees announced Friday, Dec. 4: Critics Choice Awards nominations Friday, Dec. 4: BAFTA Round One voting opens Friday, Dec. 4: Golden Globes nomination voting ends Sunday, Dec. 6: British Independent Film Awards Sunday, Dec. 6: Los Angeles Film Critics Association Awards announcement The Gothams have long been a launching pad for independent cinema, a place for films that might otherwise get flattened by the studio machine. In 2023, the organization scrapped its $35 million budget ceiling and opened more categories to international titles. The result is a more eclectic ballot, one that puts established auteurs and first-time filmmakers side by side. This year, that means 42 features and 25 performances across 11 categories. That makes the Gothams a natural first stop for “The Invite,” which we expect to win best feature. articles.content: Record Store Day is back in black. As you likely already know, RSD is a semiannual holiday for vinyl hounds, with the Black Friday edition being a less jam-packed adjunct to the primary event in April — meaning that, this year, for instance, there are “only” 188 titles being released, almost exactly half of the 355 exclusives that were put on sale in the spring event. Even with that lesser amount of limited-edition discs going out onto the shelves, there is truly something for everybody in this list. Or, to put it another way: If you can’t find anything that grabs you in this lineup, then, to quote Leonard Cohen, you don’t really care for music, do ya? Our best guess is that there will not be utter pandemonium in the indie shops or in the lines outside this Black Friday morning, if only because of the lack of a Taylor, Olivia or Billie title this time. Which does not mean that there will not still be a healthy contingent of young people joining the veteran vinyl geeks in the checkout lines. In an interview published earlier in the week in Variety , RSD co-founder Michael Kurtz said that the majority of customers for Record Store Day events are under 35. That may continue to be the case as this one has titles from hot and/or younger-skewing artists or franchises including Noah Kahan, Katseye, Sombr and the “Wicked” and “Kpop Demon Hunters” films. That said, boomers are still gonna boom, and they, Gen-X-ers, millennials and others who have a taste for classic rock, soul and jazz — meaning every generation, really — will find something to salivate over in a list of vintage material that includes Bruce Springsteen, Prince, Joni Mitchell, Miles Davis, Billy Joel, Bill Withers, Art Blakey and even a collectible from the Beatles that was added to the list after it was first announced in October. articles.content: A judge on Wednesday blocked the Federal Communications Commission from seeking early license renewals from ABC stations, finding that the network has faced a “campaign of retaliation” for its protected speech. The FCC ordered Disney-owned ABC in April to file renewal applications for its eight owned stations, including WABC-TV New York, KABC-TV Los Angeles and WLS-TV Chicago. The FCC’s action came a few days after Jimmy Kimmel, the network’s late night host, joked that the First Lady had “a glow like an expectant widow,” which prompted President Trump to call for Kimmel’s firing. articles.content: Brad Pitt has settled his legal battle with ex-wife Angelina Jolie over the sale of her stake in the couple’s winery in France. Pitt sued Jolie in 2022, accusing her of selling her 50% share in Château Miraval to a subsidiary of Stoli, the Russian spirits company, without Pitt’s approval. The litigation drew attention to Jolie’s allegation that Pitt abused her and the couple’s children on a private plane in 2016, precipitating the couple’s divorce. articles.content: “ The Hawk ,” a Will Ferrell golf comedy that debuted just this summer, has been canceled by Netflix and will not return for a second season, an individual with knowledge told IndieWire. Ferrell co-created the series in which he plays a former top golfer who is now trying to return to the tour. And while it figured to be a tentpole series for Netflix, one that carried possibly the most expensive budget for a comedy series on Netflix and reunited Ferrell with his “SNL” co-star Molly Shannon and co-creator Harper Steele, it didn’t connect with critics or audiences. “The Hawk” spent just three weeks on Netflix’s Top 10 when it debuted back in July, topping out at #2 in its second week on Netflix with just 6.2 million views. Ferrell’s vulgar, loudly-dressed golfer with a personalized visor and big mess of bleached blonde hair played a lot like some of Ferrell’s other string of sports comedies throughout the years. James will produce and Gala Gordon will co-produce for Parodos Productions. Molly Sims is also producing along with Gaby McCormick for Something Happy Productions. No writer is currently attached. A Sunday Times and New York Times bestseller, The Hunting Party follows a group of old Oxford friends whose holiday reunion at a remote hunting lodge turns deadly when a blizzard leaves them snowbound, and one of them is found murdered. The novel established Foley as a leading voice in commercial thrillers and was shortlisted for Crime & Thriller Book of the Year at the British Book Awards. Not to be confused with the NBC procedural drama of the same name created by J.J. Bailey that aired for two seasons between 2025 and 2026, Foley’s The Hunting Party was published in December 2018. Foley will executive produce. Foley has sold over 12 million copies worldwide and is a New York Times and Sunday Times No. 1 bestselling author. Other novels of hers that have been optioned for development include The Paris Apartment and The Midnight Feast , though neither adaptation has been made. Director of Production Development Christine Sun will oversee the project for the Studio. The first title from Yuasa’s new studio ame pippin unveiled images to The Hollywood Reporter of the main characters from the animated adaptation of Banana Yoshimoto’s novel, The Life of Daisy, and original illustrations by Yoshitomo Nara. articles.summary: He also worked with Steven Spielberg on ‘Jurassic Park,’ ‘Minority Report,’ ‘The Color Purple’ and ‘Twister’ and headed production at Amblin Entertainment.
articles.content: Gerald R. Molen, the Oscar-winning producer who teamed with Steven Spielberg on films including Schindler’s List , Jurassic Park and Minority Report , has died. He was 91. A longtime resident of Bigfork, Montana, Molen died Monday, his great-niece Rachel Lorraine Pullan announced . Molen first worked with Spielberg as a unit production manager on The Color Purple (1985), after which the filmmaker offered him his first producing gig, as an associate producer on *batteries not included (1987). Molen’s producing credits outside of Spielberg and Amblin included the best picture winner Rain Man (1988), Days of Thunder (1990), The Other Side of Heaven (2001), Just Like Heaven (2005), The Meg (2018) and Meg 2: The Trench (2023). Gerald Robert Molen was born on Jan. 6, 1935, in Great Falls, Montana. articles.content: Cédric Klapisch will receive an honorary César Award at the 52nd César Awards, France ‘s equivalent of the Oscars. The 64-year-old director is best known in France for his L’Auberge Espagnole ( The Spanish Apartment ) trilogy, which followed a group of European students sharing a Barcelona flat. articles.title: NBC Pulls Ad Criticizing U.S. Military Aid to Israel After Backlash, Reviews Approval Process
articles.summary: The ad aired during Wednesday's 'SNL' Thanksgiving special without senior NBC management's knowledge, a source familiar with the situation tells The Hollywood Reporter.
articles.content: NBC will not air a controversial anti-Israel advertisement again after it drew backlash for airing during Wednesday night’s Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special. NBCUniversal will now evaluate its advertising approval process to ensure appropriate levels of review. The 30-second advertisement, titled “Every Three Seconds,” shows a young girl saving money for a year by doing yard work, including mowing the lawn, blowing leaves and shoveling snow, until she raises $400 to buy a bicycle. articles.title: TV Ratings: ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Records Another Huge Finale
articles.summary: Early ratings are at a 12-year high among adults 18-49 and even with last year in total viewers.
articles.content: The season 35 finale of Dancing With the Stars capped off a season of big ratings with the show’s best numbers of the fall. Early Nielsen ratings have the finale — which aired live coast to coast, a first for DWTS — averaging 9.2 million viewers, on par with preliminary numbers for last season’s final episode . The season 34 finale ended up at 9.43 million viewers after the addition of Nielsen’s big data component; final same-day numbers for Tuesday’s show will be available after Thanksgiving. The DWTS finale also scored the show’s best rating among adults 18-49 in more than a decade: It’s currently at 2.38 (equivalent to about 3.24 million people in the demographic), subject to adjustments. That’s the highest rating for a Dancing With the Stars episode since the season 19 finale in 2014 — when current host Alfonso Ribeiro won the mirror ball trophy — and the highest mark for a regularly scheduled network entertainment show (i.e., not a special like the Oscars or Grammys) since an episode of The Masked Singer in April 2020. The finale also scored a 15-year high among adults under 35 with a 2.86 rating — an almost unheard-of number for anything outside of live sports in the current broadcast environment. Pending updates for the finale, season 35 of DWTS averaged 7.19 million viewers, up about 11 percent from last year. The show’s 1.59 rating among adults 18-49 is up by almost 20 percent year to year. The latter number ranks first among all network shows this fall, excluding live sports, and leads second-place Survivor (0.86 rating) by a canyon-sized 86 percent margin. Should that hold, it would be the largest gap between a first- and second-place show in the 18-49 demo since the beginning of Nielsen’s electronic measurement in 1991. ABC says viewers cast a record-setting 86 million votes during the finale, up from 72 million for the season 34 closer. DWTS also generated the most social media engagements of any primetime program Tuesday.

articles.content: Christopher Nolan ‘s adaptation of Homer’s “ The Odyssey ” was one of the most awe-inspiring cinematic achievements of 2026, an epic worthy of comparison with the grandiose visions of David Lean and Stanley Kubrick . Yet what interested cinematographer Hoyte van Hoytema was less the story’s vast scale than the details of the human faces inhabiting the film ‘s sweeping vistas. “We never really treated it in an epic way,” van Hoytema told IndieWire. “Even though we all know ‘ The Odyssey ‘ and understand the scale of the story, making some sort of a tourist film was never on our agenda. It was the characters and the visceral sense of their experience that we were interested in, so even standing in the most crazy places in the world — on mountaintops or wherever — we were never motivated by the landscapes. The settings take care of creating the scale and scope of the film — our perspective on the story was a very intimate one.” Related Stories Forget Photorealism: How ‘Wildwood’ Made Its Handmade Digital Artistry Visible ‘Cliff Booth’ Brings Back a Fan-Favorite ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood’ Face Given that, van Hoytema tried not to be seduced by the beauty of his surroundings if it didn’t serve the emotional experience. “It was less about showing how beautiful a beach was than about showing how shitty those men felt when they were on the beach,” he said, noting that a key tool in getting across the characters’ internal feelings was shooting the film entirely in IMAX. “Shooting an entire film in IMAX has been a pursuit of ours for quite a long time now, and we’ve been tweaking the lenses and tweaking the cameras in order to get there,” van Hoytema said. “We’ve managed to wrangle the equipment and technology around it to enable us to be right there next to you, looking straight into your eyes.” This again plays into that idea of intimacy versus scale, which was something van Hoytema and Nolan had experimented with in “Oppenheimer.” In that film, IMAX was used not only

articles.summary: WETA VFX Supervisors Dan Macarin and Sabine Laimer tell IndieWire how they matched the tones and textures of Laika's stop-motion film.
articles.content: WETA FX has been called upon to do visual effects for everything, from orc armies to superheroes, alien planetscapes to the innards of a whale . On each project, they have to match the movie’s consistency. The goal is to make sure that the VFX blends perfectly into the overall visual style, not so unlike a certain Springfield dad creeping into a hedge. Meeting that challenge often means the teams at WETA match and then build on live-action footage to get as close to a photorealistic look as possible. But adding digital effects to the wonderful world of stop-motion animation , as with “ Wildwood ,” WETA FX got to have more fun with creating a world that looks as textured and handmade as the puppets designed and animated by Laika Studios . Related Stories ‘Cliff Booth’ Brings Back a Fan-Favorite ‘Once Upon a Time in Hollywood’ Face How Disney’s ‘Hexed’ Reinvents the Witch Through Animation “Everybody was super stoked about this film because it’s so different from what we usually do. People got to be artists,” VFX supervisor Sabine Laimer told IndieWire. “We’re really good at making effects invisible, but here we could actually showcase the artistry. All of our people here loved it.” This applies to the way that WETA helped intensify battle sequences, the way they expanded sets so that they feel as fast as the impassible woods where most of “ Wildwood ” takes place, and the way they were able to match cinematographer Caleb Deschanel’s lighting to bring a unity to the digital and puppetry work within individual scenes. When designing the ivy that Alexandra (Carey Mulligan) seeks to control and that Prue (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) seeks to pacify, WETA’s digital leaves weren’t meant to mimic real leaves in nature.
